family: OIG speaker-program alert & CIA promotional controls

source.document: HHS-OIG Special Fraud Alert: Speaker Programs (Nov 2020)

rules.rule_text: Speaker programs should present substantive information; alcohol or meals exceeding modest value are suspect.
rules.verbatim_quote: Alcohol is available or a meal exceeding modest value is provided to the attendees of the program

detection.logic: On meta.program: fail if alcohol==true, meal_cost_per_head > company cap, or educational_minutes < meta.min_minutes.

source.document: HHS-OIG Special Fraud Alert: Speaker Programs (Nov 2020)

rules.rule_text: Venues not conducive to education (restaurants, entertainment or sports venues) are suspect.
rules.verbatim_quote: The program is held at a location that is not conducive to the exchange of educational information (e.g., restaurants or entertainment or sports venues)

detection.logic: meta.program.venue_type in {restaurant, bar, sports, entertainment, resort} -> fail.

source.document: HHS-OIG Special Fraud Alert: Speaker Programs (Nov 2020)
source.section: Suspect characteristics (repeat attendance; attendees without business reason)

rules.rule_text: Repeat attendance on the same topic and attendees with no legitimate business reason (friends, family, own-practice staff) are suspect.
rules.verbatim_quote: HCPs attend programs on the same or substantially the same topics more than once

detection.logic: meta.program.attendees: fail on repeat attendee for same topic within the tracking window, or attendee.relationship in {spouse, family, friend, speaker_practice_staff}.

source.document: HHS-OIG Special Fraud Alert: Speaker Programs (Nov 2020)

rules.rule_text: Speaker selection driven by sales/ROI and compensation above fair market value are suspect.
rules.verbatim_quote: The company pays HCP speakers more than fair market value for the speaking service

detection.logic: meta.program.speaker: fail if selected_by in {sales, marketing} or roi_used, or honorarium > fmv_cap.

source.document: HHS-OIG Special Fraud Alert: Speaker Programs (Nov 2020)
source.section: Suspect characteristics (little substantive content; no new information)

rules.rule_text: Programs with little substantive content or no recent new information (many repeats on same topic) are suspect.
rules.verbatim_quote: The company sponsors speaker programs where little or no substantive information is actually presented

detection.question: Does the speaker deck/program convey substantive, current educational content justifying the program?
detection.pass_anchor: Substantive content tied to new data/indication or bona fide educational need.
detection.fail_anchor: Thin content, mostly promotional or repeated with no new information.

source.document: Corporate Integrity Agreement between HHS-OIG and Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation (Jun 30 2020) - used as a representative pharma CIA
source.status: CIA (binding on that company only; typical of pharma CIAs)

rules.rule_text: Promotional, reimbursement and disease-state materials must be reviewed by qualified regulatory, medical and/or legal personnel before external dissemination.
rules.verbatim_quote: review of promotional, reimbursement, and disease state materials and information intended to be disseminated outside Novartis by appropriate qualified personnel (such as regulatory, medical, and/or legal personnel)

detection.logic: meta.approvals must include medical, legal and regulatory sign-offs with dates on or before meta.first_use_date.

source.document: Corporate Integrity Agreement between HHS-OIG and Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation (Jun 30 2020) - used as a representative pharma CIA
source.status: CIA (binding on that company only; typical of pharma CIAs)

rules.rule_text: Companies under a CIA monitor speaker programs and field activity (controls, live/recorded observation, reviews).

detection.logic: meta.program.monitored or recorded flag required where company policy demands it.
